A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniTime research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original temporal-grounding and VideoQA experiments, module and robustness analyses, and additional model-size and architecture experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds closed-model comparisons, broader backbone evaluations, grounding-consistency tests and additional ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.3 retain adaptive frame scaling, timestamp interleaving, hierarchical inference, the autoregressive objective and video-centric training. Additional backbone experiments and explanations do not document a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The training datasets, five main grounding benchmarks and four VideoQA benchmarks remain unchanged. Appendix D adds Charades-CON and ActivityNet-CON evaluations involving paraphrased queries and shifted moments, extending test conditions within existing video domains.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Qwen2-VL-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B baselines. New Table 5 compares Gemini-2.5-Flash/Pro, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4o and Seed1.5-VL. Tables 6 and 10 further add InternVL2.5 baselines and consistency comparisons involving Gemini 1.5 Flash, Video-LLaMA and TimeChat with and without VTune.

E3.justification: V2 introduces random-subset closed-model evaluation that excludes outputs without timestamps, consistency evaluation across three paraphrases and shifted moments, and controlled processing, threshold and token-budget sweeps. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the original training defaults and benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds consistency testing, resizing-versus-compression controls, timestamp-versus-position-encoding ablations, and sensitivity analyses for both frame thresholds and token budget. Backbone analysis expands to InternVL2.5. The earlier Qwen size/type studies are partly incorporated into Section 3.4, rather than being entirely new experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Table 10's bracketed values are relative consistency scores; averaging across three paraphrases defines an evaluation metric rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Shared main benchmark, module-ablation, robustness and VideoQA scores remain unchanged. Tables 5–6 and 10–15 add substantial results, including Charades-STA mIoU of 63.15 versus 44.85 for timestamp insertion versus dense position encodings. V1 Table 9's Qwen2.5-VL UniTime results on ANet-Captions, QVHighlights and TaCoS are omitted. New subset results do not establish improvements over earlier full-benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds a mathematical specification of rephrased grounding consistency using IoU between predictions for original and paraphrased queries, averaged over three variants. The original task formulation, scaling equations, sequence construction and training loss remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: universal grounding through timestamp interleaving and adaptive scaling, hierarchical inference, efficient training, benchmark performance and downstream VideoQA benefits. Additional experiments support these retained claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning balanced short/long-video performance against closed models, consistency relative to VTune, and accuracy-versus-computation tradeoffs for processing strategies and thresholds. The existing limitations concerning task specialization, reasoning capabilities and fixed segment lengths remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds training-cost information: Table 11 reports 21, 12 and 24.5 hours for processing alternatives, and the text reports five additional days for short-video token compression in UniTime-Full. It also explains threshold routing and the hardware-imposed token ceiling. Existing optimization details, prompts and project link are retained.

R1.justification: Eight references are added, covering newly evaluated models and grounding-consistency research. Section 3.6 and Appendix D explicitly position UniTime against VTune's consistency-oriented training. The broader related-work taxonomy and earlier citations remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 inserts closed-model and flexibility subsections, moves and reworks model ablations, reorganizes the later appendices, and adds cross-references, acknowledgements and the conference designation. Most existing introduction, method, related-work and conclusion prose is retained.

P2.justification: The table presentation expands substantially with closed-model, consistency, processing, encoding and hyperparameter displays. The separate model-size/type tables are recast into Table 6's baseline-versus-UniTime layout, Table 3 gains rows, and several displays move. The eight existing figures retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked direct controls isolating timestamp encoding and resizing versus token compression. V2 supplies these controls and sensitivity/cost evidence in Tables 11–15, while Table 6 extends validation beyond Qwen and Appendix D adds consistency testing. This substantially strengthens support for central design and generality claims. Benefits are tempered by omitted cross-dataset backbone results and weaknesses in the new closed-model comparison: unspecified subset sizes, exclusion of untimestamped outputs, and a Seed1.5-VL prose score of 72.2 conflicting with Table 5's 73.69. These issues limit that comparison but do not outweigh the stronger component-level validation.
